Can we use a https://godoc.org/golang.org/x/sync/singleflight#Group per shard instead?

Why?

On Tue, Oct 8, 2019, 7:40 PM Mike Danese <notifications@github.com> wrote:

> Can we a https://godoc.org/golang.org/x/sync/singleflight per shard
> instead?
>
> —
> You are receiving this because you were mentioned.
> Reply to this email directly, view it on GitHub
> <https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/83519?email_source=notifications&email_token=AAE6BFTKRJBUYR2INKHSCJ3QNVADNA5CNFSM4I5VOTTKYY3PNVWWK3TUL52HS4DFVREXG43VMVBW63LNMVXHJKTDN5WW2ZLOORPWSZGOEAWKA5Q#issuecomment-539795574>,
> or mute the thread
> <https://github.com/notifications/unsubscribe-auth/AAE6BFR5SITUI7KNQHTF2OLQNVADNANCNFSM4I5VOTTA>
> .
>

It does what we are trying to do here and the complexity is contained within a library maintained by the Go team. We can protect this section:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6d97d36fbb5a52e9e7520fb326283a53ba1570a4/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/authentication/token/cache/cached_token_authenticator.go#L78-L88

With a singleflight.Group and get the same result.

That's not really an improvement, e.g. what happens if a call never
returns? As written, the cache bounds the number of callers who get stuck
in that situation.

I'd consider that more carefully if it were actually in the standard
library, the x libraries haven't been uniformly high quality in my
experience, maybe they're better now, but I'm not inclined to switch. Using
code we don't have to own isn't automatically better...

Anyway the cache as it exists in the code encourages this bad usage
pattern, I either don't want the cache to be in a library I'm on the hook
for at all, or I want it to give you the option of not using the included
foot gun.

Yup, there's always a tradeoff.

> I'd consider that more carefully if it were actually in the standard library,

The x/sync/singleflight package is a mirror of src/internal/singleflight. It's used to share lookups in the Go DNS resolver:

https://github.com/golang/go/blob/fac3b5d05ecf31a2491949cc905312a34e272ae8/src/net/lookup.go#L149-L152

So we're actually already using it in apiserver, controller-manager, kubectl, etc compiled with CGO_ENABLED=0... whenever we do a DNS lookup.

> what happens if a call never returns?

https://godoc.org/golang.org/x/sync/singleflight#DoChan returns a result chan that a caller can select on with a ctx.Done(). https://godoc.org/golang.org/x/sync/singleflight#Forget allows a caller to abandon a stuck lookup. src/internal/singleflight also has ForgetUnshared that hasn't been exported yet but is used in the resolver for this situation:

https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2197321db1dd997165c0091ba2bcb3b6be7633d0/src/net/lookup.go#L277-L284

I personally still think it is better to fix the cache. If you can point to a concrete problem in my implementation... ? But right now it just feels like more work to switch to that for no clear purpose.

Fixing it in the cache means only one lock to contend on.

I do want to modify my interface slightly, I think I can use context better. (than either my current code or the inflight one)
hm, actually it's hard to improve on my interface since context isn't testable (doesn't support injecting a clock for testing).

> If you can point to a concrete problem in my implementation... ?

I can give the change a thorough review, but assuming that all issues with software can be fixed, this devolves to the arguments for and against using external dependencies. The code introduced in this change is fairly complex and we'll have to maintain it. singleflight seems like a solid alternative that fits what we need here.

Other than that, this change is currently coupled with the LRUExpiringCache. I added some reasons in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83375#issuecomment-540243511 why we might want to move off LRU for the token cache. Decoupling the current implementation is also something that we could do without introducing an external dependency.

> hm, actually it's hard to improve on my interface since context isn't testable (doesn't support injecting a clock for testing).

Not sure I follow this.

I have unpushed changes that address some of those comments, but I would be even happier to delete the LRU cache completely as you mentioned elsewhere, I don't actually trust the thing it depends on.

I will send this benchmark in a separate PR and hold on to this one for a bit.

issue_context.title: Authentication token cache can live-lock
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.16/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/authentication/token/cache/cached_token_authenticator.go#L70-L91

This code releases the lock to do the actual work. This means if there are N simultaneous requests for a token, apiserver will look it up N times. If that happens in parallel, OK, maybe it's not the end of the world, but as it happens it might not. Even if we didn't have a [self-client](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/22423/files#diff-36e1d7088209b1ab6ff878b18bb35210R262) rate limit, etcd might be sluggish or serialize requests, or the webhook could be slow...

Since this cache holds results for a maximum of 10 seconds and we had a 50 qps rate limit for looking them up, in reality, only 500 items could be in the cache at any one given time, even though the cache could hold 4096 entries.

With a poor request order, just a few more than 500 items can therefore to trigger a serious issue (most requests making token-auth calls time out and leak a go routine due to our behavior on global time out).

With a pessimal request order and pessimal set of tokens, just a few more than 128 are necessary due to the way this is sharded into 32 caches of 128.

1.14 and 1.16 both contain changes that effectively prevent this behavior, and we've back-ported [removing the self-client rate limit](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/80465) to 1.13. But, those just address a trigger for this; I think defense-in-depth demands we actually fix the cache, too.

So, this issue has two requests:
* Fix the cache, such that two simultaneous requests for an un-cached token will share work.
* Make the cache bigger and/or make the 4096 limit shared between shards rather than divided into 128 for each, which is too small.

/sig auth
/priority important-soon

If finalValue stores nil to represent omission, do we still need finalValueOmitted ?
Someone might deliberately store a nil.

Should we only cancel this if the lookup is not shared? If the first caller closes their connection to the apiserver, the result (error context canceled?) will be returned to any other callers waiting for the same lookup. Ideally the lookup should return to other waiters even if the first caller bails.
It's probably simpler and less error prone to have goroutines waiting on `<-ce.wait` handle their own timeouts rather than requiring that lookupFuncs properly abort.

computationTime should be a cache intrinsic, and not passed in by the caller. Callers share lookups so the lookup should run in a detached context. For example, right now if someone calls with computationTime of `1*time.Hour` and the next person calls with computationTIme of `1*time.Second`, the second caller blocks for `1*time.Hour`.
